scalars.scalar_value: As needed, Monday-Friday 5:00am-1:30pm, and rotating weekends and holidays

items.item_text: California Driver's License (subject to DMV Pull)

In this role you will be responsible for the ordering, management, and distribution of procedural supplies throughout the distribution of medical supplies throughout the Medical Center and/or Ambulatory clinics ensuring the clinical staff have all the supplies they need for patient care.
Work closely with the clinical staff to adjust targeted inventory levels based on current usage to best align with upcoming procedures.
Distribution of supplies and equipment as assigned within all facilities at UCLA Health System.
Deliveries may include driving university vehicles to transport supplies and equipment to UCLA community clinics (subject to DMV Pull).
Update supply formulary and targeted par levels within supply management software.
Place supply replenishment orders using a handheld device or supply management software.
Maintain and update ordering bar codes on supply bin locations.
Receive / transport supply orders from dock and reconcile packing slips against ordered quantities.
Identify inventory cost reduction opportunities based on usage, alternatives, and expiring product.
Communicate inventory availability using back ordered and on-order bin location stickers.
Assemble custom supply packs by procedure type to help expedite surgical preparations.
Provide inventory on-hand counts to support department weekly back ordered items reports.
Assist clinical staff in reconciling supplies used during procedures for billing purposes.
Willingness to comply with healthcare regulations for infection control, including masking.
Self-starter with effective time management and a high degree of accuracy and attention to detail.
Flexibility to changes in workload, assignments, and schedules across different shifts and weekends.
Organized to stay current in required HR online competency classes on policy and safety between tasks.
Consistently maintain a safe, clean working environment and report unsafe acts or conditions.
A high proficiency in English to articulate issues, concerns, and responses verbally and electronically.
Actively participates in Quality Management and PIE programs.; adheres to Materials Management and UCLA policies/procedures.

the final candidate who accepts an offer of employment will be required to disclose if they have been subject to any final administrative or judicial decisions within the last seven years determining that they committed any misconduct; or have filed an appeal of a finding of substantiated misconduct with a previous employer.
Ability to push and pull up to 150 pounds, and lift up to 50 pounds. ability to use computer and mobile scanner.
Ability to maintain a positive attitude and work as a team in a fast-paced environment
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with clinical interruptions for supply requests.
Ability to attend all workshops, classes, drills, etc as requested.
